gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: In 2015, Syndicate 1084 reported a prior year reserve release of GBP 95.7 million, representing 6.06% of its opening gross claims outstanding. This release was primarily driven by favourable claims development on attritional losses, predominantly within the Energy, Casualty, and Treaty Divisions. The year also saw various catastrophe events, including the Tianjin Port explosions (net loss GBP 13.5m) and UK floods (net loss GBP 4.5m), as well as other natural catastrophes like Hurricane Patricia, winter storms in the US and Canada, and European floods. Prior year events from 2014, such as Japan snowfall, US hailstorms/tornadoes, and Hurricane Odile, had minimal impact on reserve movements in 2015.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: During 2015 Syndicate 1084 recorded a net release of prior year claims reserves of GBP 95.7m (a c.6.06% release relative to opening gross claims outstanding of GBP 1,579.2m). The releases were driven predominantly by favourable claims development on attritional losses across the Energy, Casualty and Treaty divisions. Specific 2015 events quantified in the reserves note include the Tianjin port explosion (current estimated net claims ~GBP 14.8m) and UK flood events (net ~GBP 4.5m); several 2014 events (Japan snowfall, US hail/tornado, Hurricane Odile) are noted as having small remaining impacts (each below GBP 10m). The report does not quantify reserve movements by line of business, only noting which divisions were predominantly responsible for the prior year releases.

gpt-5-mini.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding and technical reserves figures taken from the Technical Reserves note (table) and Movement in prior years statement. Prior year release amount (GBP 95.7m) is explicitly stated in the Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding note. The report does not provide per-line quantified prior year reserve movements; LOB attributions are reported qualitatively (Energy, Casualty, Treaty). Some named events have syndicate-level estimated amounts (Tianjin, UK floods) while many market events are discussed qualitatively without syndicate-specific monetary impacts. Page numbers are inferred from the report's notes pagination and may vary by formatting.
